insights.title: CSS Token Aliasing via var(): Alias Tokens Inherit Dark-Mode Overrides Without Extra Declarations
insights.content: In `gui/public/css/styles.css`, new semantic design tokens can be added by aliasing existing tokens with `var(--existing-token)` in the `:root` block (e.g., `--badge-credential-set: var(--badge-clean)`). When the dark-mode theme block redefines `--badge-clean`, the alias token `--badge-credential-set` automatically resolves to the dark-mode value via the CSS cascade — no additional dark-mode declaration is needed for the alias. This was confirmed in WP-003 (which required a rework pass specifically because this pattern was missed on the first implementation). Use this approach for any future badge or status variant that maps 1:1 to an existing token colour.

insights.title: Server Test Helpers Convention: Every File in __tests__/helpers/ Requires Both **Consumers** and **Exports** JSDoc Sections
insights.content: Shared test helpers in `src/server/__tests__/helpers/` must follow the `mock-http.ts` convention: a file-level JSDoc block with both a `**Consumers**` section (listing which test files import from this helper) and an `**Exports**` section (enumerating public exports with brief descriptions). The `**Exports**` section was initially missing from `mock-error-log-manager.ts` (WP-004) and was flagged as a documentation-forward by the Reviewer before being added. Without both sections the helper's public API is non-discoverable for contributors unfamiliar with the directory.
